subject: Clarify Exhibit B packaging anchors and requested redline
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novushealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-23T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exhibit B — packaging anchors / caps and requested clarifications

Aditya,

Thanks for the call this morning. Novus procurement reviewed Exhibit B and has three items they need clarified before they can route to legal for signature:

1) The ‘Annualized Commit Floor’ language — procurement is concerned the current floor exposure is too high in Q1 of the term if utilization ramps slowly. Can we add a short-term soft floor (first 3 months) or a delayed true-up?

2) The cap / burst language under Section 2.3 — they want to confirm whether burst capacity charges apply pro-rata when we autoscale for short spikes. If yes, they want a min-billing increment defined (e.g., 5 minutes).

3) Packaging mapping for the ‘embedding’ SKU — Novus needs a clear mapping table from usage metric to pricing band so their billing system can reconcile.

I've attached a marked-up Exhibit B (ExhibitB_Novus_markup_v1.docx) with line notes and suggested edits. Also copied Novus legal (contracts@novushealth.com) who will supply a formal redline if procurement and product agree.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 3-month soft floor and add a pro-rata burst increment? If not, please propose an operational fallback we can present.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morales
VP, Strategic Procurement — Novus Health

Attachments: ExhibitB_Novus_markup_v1.docx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novushealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-23T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit B — packaging anchors / caps and requested clarifications

Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the markup. Looping in Priyom (sales ops) and Marissa (contracts/product) so we can propose concrete language.

Short answers up front: we are open to a time-limited soft floor for the ramp period and can define a minimum billing increment for burst charge behavior. For the embedding SKU mapping we can provide a mapping table and a reconciliation worksheet.

Proposal:
- Redwood to accept a 3-month soft floor for the first quarter, with a true-up at the end of month three based on actual usage.
- Burst billing: define a 5-minute minimum increment; bill fractional token consumption pro-rata within that increment.
- Packaging mapping: we will attach a reconciliation spreadsheet that maps embedding units to the pricing bands and include it as an annex to Exhibit B.

Marissa / Priyom — can you draft redline language for Exhibit B that implements the above? If possible, include an opt-out clause for Novus if a formal true-up is unacceptable.

I propose we target a formal redline back to Novus by EOD tomorrow so they can take to legal.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for the markup. I've attached an initial operational worksheet (pricing-schedule-Novus.xlsx) that maps embedding units -> band -> per-unit fee and shows an example true-up calculation. High-level notes:

- Soft floor: we can implement a 3-month soft floor where the ‘floor charge’ is capped at 50% of the committed floor for months 1–3, with catch-up true-up at month 3 based on aggregate usage in months 1–3. That reduces cash exposure for Novus during ramp.

- Burst billing: we recommend a 5-minute minimum billing increment for burst capacity and then per-token billing thereafter (rounded to nearest cent). We include an example line item to show how a 10-minute spike would be billed.

- Packaging mapping: see the ‘SKU reconciliation’ tab in the attached workbook. We can include this sheet as Annex 1 to Exhibit B.

If Novus legal prefers different thresholds (e.g., 60% cap vs 50%) we're open to negotiation, but the 50% is the operationally reasonable starting point.

Attachment: pricing-schedule-Novus.xlsx (worksheet: SKU reconciliation + true-up examples)

Next steps: Marissa, can you translate the 3 bullets above into contract language that we can send back as a redline?

—Priyom
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Novus Health Legal <contracts@novushealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@novushealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-25T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit B — formal redline (preliminary) 

Aditya / Team,

Per procurement's request, attached are proposed redlines to Exhibit B (we've included comments where Novus legal has policy constraints). High-level must-haves from our side: clarity on the floor true-up mechanism, a defined minimum billing increment for burst charges, and an explicit reconciliation annex for SKUs to prevent downstream disputes.

Below are the exact edits Novus legal proposes (excerpt):

--- Proposed language excerpt (Novus legal) ---
Section 1.1 (Annualized Commit Floor): 
"For the first ninety (90) days following Effective Date, Customer's Monthly Minimum Charge shall be limited to fifty percent (50%) of the then-applicable Monthly Minimum Charge as set forth in the Order Form. Customer shall remain liable for the aggregate Monthly Minimum Charge for the initial ninety (90) day period; however, Redwood shall permit a one-time true-up at the end of said period, applied to align billed charges with actual usage. Any shortfall shall be invoiced in the month following the 90-day true-up."

Section 2.3 (Burst Capacity Billing): 
"Burst capacity shall be billed in minimum increments of five (5) minutes. Charges incurred within a billing increment shall be calculated pro rata based on actual token consumption during the increment. Exceptions for automated scaling anomalies shall be addressed under the Operations SLA and crediting policy."

Annex A (SKU Reconciliation): 
"An SKU Reconciliation table shall be attached to Exhibit B as Annex A. The parties agree that the Annex A table is the authoritative mapping for purposes of invoicing. Any discrepancy between usage telemetry and Annex A will be resolved per the dispute resolution procedure in Section X."
--- end excerpt ---

Comments: Novus legal asks that the 90-day true-up language explicitly permit a one-time invoice for the shortfall. They also want the Annex A clause to include a tie to dispute resolution to avoid prolonged billing disputes.

Please review and confirm whether Redwood can accept the exact wording above or propose alternate contractual language. We are aiming to complete review and move to signature by Aug 31.

Regards,
Sophia Kim
Counsel, Novus Health
contracts@novushealth.com

Attachment referenced: Novus_ExhibitB_redline_comments.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: contracts@novushealth.com, Elena Morales <elena.morales@novushealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-26T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit B — formal redline (preliminary)

Sophia / Elena — thanks, this is clear and actionable. Redwood accepts the commercial intent in your excerpts with one small operational tweak and one drafting clarification:

1) Operational tweak (billing increment exception): we will agree the 5-minute minimum increment as proposed, but include an exception that if an autoscale event is corrected within the cloud provider's monitoring window and results in measurable excess allocation (i.e., a known scaling loop), Redwood will evaluate and credit the overage outside of normal billing. We propose the following parenthetical: "(except for automated scaling anomalies reasonably identified and credited under Redwood's Operations SLA)."

2) Drafting clarification (true-up invoicing timing): to align with Redwood's billing cycles, we propose invoicing any shortfall identified in the 90-day true-up in the second billing cycle following the true-up (i.e., allow a 30-day processing window). Suggested replacement sentence: "Any shortfall shall be invoiced in the second billing cycle following the 90-day true-up."

I've attached a clean redline implementing Novus wording with these two edits (ExhibitB_Redwood_response_v2.docx). If Novus is comfortable with the two changes, we can finalize Exhibit B and produce an updated Order Form for signature.

Next steps: Elena, if procurement confirms acceptability, can Novus legal confirm by EOD Aug 27 so we can hit signature by Aug 31? We'll prepare a DocuSign packet once we get sign-off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Contracts & Product Compliance — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: ExhibitB_Redwood_response_v2.docx
